comments.content: The new `test_animimg_set_src_reverse` only asserts that `animimg` is non-NULL, which is already guaranteed by `setUp()`. It therefore passes even if `lv_animimg_set_src_reverse` is broken (e.g. if it were implemented identically to `lv_animimg_set_src`), so the reverse behavior of the newly split API is effectively untested. Assert the observable state instead (source pointer/count), and ideally the reversed animation direction.

comments.content: `lv_animimg_set_src_reverse()` duplicates the whole body of `lv_animimg_set_src()` (same dsc/pic_count assignment), only differing in the animation range. Any future fix in the setter (e.g. bounds check on `num`, updating the currently displayed frame) would have to be applied twice and can easily be forgotten. Suggest delegating to `lv_animimg_set_src()` and only overriding the animation values.

It would also help to document the relationship with `lv_animimg_set_src()` (calling it later resets the direction to forward) so users know the two calls are mutually exclusive. Also note the stray double space after `*`.

comments.content: The only thing that makes this API distinct from `lv_animimg_set_src()` is the direction of the anim values (`num -> 0`), yet the accompanying test only asserts that the object pointer is non-NULL, which is always true. A regression in the direction (e.g. accidentally keeping `0 -> num`) would therefore pass the tests silently. Consider adding a behavioural assertion, e.g. start the animation and check that the first displayed source is the last entry of `dsc`.

Now, is there a concern the reverse animation doesn't actually start from the last image because `lv_anim_set_values(num, 0)` where start value equals pic_count is out of bounds? Consider `index_change` is invoked with idx values through the animation. In lv_anim, on start, `lv_anim_start` sets `a->current_value`... Let me check lv_anim_start: in v9, `lv_anim_start()` computes and applies the start value if `early_apply` is true (default true?). Let me check `lv_anim_set_early_apply` default in lv_anim_init. If early apply default true, at t=0 value = num → clamped → index num-1. Good.

However there's a subtle thing: with reverse direction the last image (index num-1) is displayed at start AND at halfway? Values: from num to 0 over duration. index = round(value)? The exec cb receives int32_t computed via `lv_map`: value = start + (end-start)*t/duration, so first tick maybe num-1 or num. index num and num-1 both clamp to num-1 → index num-1 gets shown during two frame intervals (a bit longer). Minor.

This could cause the first frame to be wrong. But again pre-existing pattern and probably out of scope (num > 127 unlikely). Skip.
